reasons: The opinion states that the liquor industry was long subject to close supervision and inspection and that Congress had broad authority to fashion standards of reasonableness for searches and seizures in that industry.
The opinion states that Congress selected a standard that did not include forcible warrantless entries and instead made refusal of admission an offense.

The facts state that Rozzo refused to unlock the storeroom, an agent broke the lock and entered, and the suit sought return and suppression of the seized liquor; the judgment was reversed, supporting the stated suppression consequence.
The authority-weight label is consistent with the lake identity fields identifying the court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus.
No treatment or currency finding is made under Lens A.
residual_risks: Lens A does not assess current treatment validity.
